FINDING A (load-bearing, for pass-1 design) — the ollama model's memory is NOT in the dispatched tree. `ollama launch pi` spawns `pi` (the client), but the model runs in an `ollama runner` process parented to `ollama serve` (the daemon, pid 67229), not to the dispatch. tools/runner's descendant walk therefore cannot see or kill the model: gemma4:12b-mlx's peak-RSS-by-PID topped out at 272 MB while its 7.7 GB model was loaded. Consequence: the host-floor guard fires on global pressure, kills the wrong (272 MB client) process, relieves nothing, then crashes. This is the per-family topology fact the spec's §3 residual check was designed to catch (for ollama the heaviest process is a daemon-owned sibling, not a descendant); measured twice (qwen orphan D14, gem12). Evidence: untracked/bakeoff/pass1-audit-round1/gemma4:12b-mlx/trailer.log (peak RSS 272 MB, host-floor cull at avail 5876 MB) and qwen3.8:27b-mlx/trailer.log (attempt-1 orphan).

FINDING B (for pass-1 cannibalization C1) — the killpg EPERM crash reproduced 4×. tools/runner:1554 `os.killpg(proc.pid, signal.SIGKILL)` raises PermissionError [Errno 1] after the host-floor guard kills the largest member; the group leader is already reaped or a member escaped its session. Reproduced: T554 tournament (qwen lane, :1505 in the old tree), T555 (D12/D13), T556 qwen (attempt 3), T556 gemma4:12b-mlx. This is the exact call site pass-1 C1 replaces; four live reproductions in one day is the strongest evidence the cannibalization step is necessary. The scoped subclaim (absent from c.zig/posix.zig) is true; the design conclusion (own extern "c" fn getsid for macOS) stands. A 'verified' statement is verifiably false — disposition D-4, must, ACCEPT.
